safe_temperature.disagreements: The FDA standard specifies a minimum internal temperature of 145°F with a 3-minute rest period for whole beef cuts (chops, roasts, steaks), which corresponds to medium doneness. Steakhouse and precision cooking sources across the notebook (Allen Brothers, Omaha Steaks, WebstaurantStore, Fit Foodie Finds) emphasize cooking steaks according to preferred doneness tiers: Rare at 120°F (cool-to-warm red center), Medium-Rare at 130°F–134°F (warm red center, perfectly rendered intramuscular marbling), Medium at 140°F–145°F (hot pink center), Medium-Well at 150°F (mostly brown center), and Well-Done at 160°F+ (firm, dry, no pink). For low-temperature precision methods (reverse sear and sous vide), steaks are removed from the initial heat 10°F to 15°F below the target temperature (e.g. 115°F–120°F for medium-rare), relying on high-heat surface searing and carryover resting to reach the final internal temperature.

methods.cut: thick-cut steaks (1.5 to 2 inches thick, e.g. cowboy ribeye, bone-in New York strip, thick filet mignon)
methods.heat: 250°F (121°C) low oven roast, finished in a smoking-hot cast-iron skillet over high heat
methods.time: 25 to 35 minutes in oven (until internal temp hits 115°F for medium-rare), followed by 45 to 90 seconds sear per side
methods.doneness: Target temperature after searing and resting reaches 130°F (medium-rare) or 140°F (medium); uniform edge-to-edge pink interior with a deep caramelized exterior crust
methods.rest: At least 5 minutes on a warm plate or board
methods.tips: Pat steaks completely dry and leave uncovered on a wire rack in the refrigerator for 2 to 24 hours to dehydrate the surface for maximum crust formation; cook on a wire rack set inside a sheet pan in the oven; sear in a high-smoke-point neutral oil; sear the outer fat cap edges for 30 seconds to render fat; baste with foaming butter, smashed garlic, and fresh rosemary/thyme during the final 30 seconds.

methods.cut: thick steaks (1.5 to 2 inches thick, ribeye, tenderloin filet mignon, strip)
methods.heat: Precision water bath at 125°F–128°F (for medium-rare) or 130°F–134°F (for medium); smoking-hot cast-iron skillet for finishing
methods.time: 2 to 4 hours in water bath (40 to 60 minutes for 1-inch steaks; up to 4 hours to tenderize fibers), followed by 1 minute sear per side
methods.doneness: 100% edge-to-edge uniform doneness with zero gray banding; deep golden-brown crust
methods.tips: Generously season both sides with coarse salt and pepper; seal in bag with 1 tablespoon of butter and a sprig of fresh herbs; remove as much air as possible; remove from bath, discard juices, and pat bone-dry with paper towels before searing for exactly 1 minute per side in smoking-hot cast iron with butter and oil.

methods.cut: flat iron steak, tenderloin filet, top sirloin filet, strip filet (1 to 1.5 inches thick)
methods.heat: Medium-high heat in heavy cast-iron skillet, optional 350°F (177°C) oven finish
methods.time: 3 to 4 minutes per side in skillet (or 2 minutes per side sear followed by 6 to 8 minutes in 350°F oven)
methods.tips: Heat skillet until oil shimmers; sear undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes to build crust; spoon melted herb butter continuously over steak to baste; transfer to 350°F oven if steak is thick to finish center without scorching surface.

methods.cut: T-bone, ribeye, porterhouse, top sirloin, strip steak (1 to 1.5 inches thick)
methods.heat: Medium to medium-high heat on charcoal or gas grill (approx. 400°F–450°F at grates)
methods.time: 4 to 6 minutes per side for 1-inch thick steak (10 to 14 minutes total)
methods.tips: Trim outside fat to 1/4-inch to prevent flare-ups; preheat grill grates thoroughly; flip only once using tongs (never pierce with a fork to avoid losing juices); let meat rest so juices redistribute away from center.

source.name: BEEF COOKERY - NDBeef & Clover Meadows Beef

methods.cut: top sirloin, ribeye, flat iron (3/4 to 1 inch thick)
methods.heat: Preheated high oven broil setting (rack positioned 3 to 4 inches from heat element)
methods.time: 3 minutes on first side, flip, and 3 minutes on second side (approx. 6 to 10 minutes total for 3/4-inch to 1-inch steak)
methods.tips: Preheat broiler for 10 minutes so oven cavity is intensely hot; place steak on a slotted broiler pan so rendering fat drips below; flip once with tongs at the halfway mark.

avoid.warning: Searing cold or wet meat: surface moisture creates a barrier of steam that prevents the Maillard reaction crust from forming; bring steak to room temperature and pat thoroughly dry.
Piercing meat with a carving fork while flipping: puncturing the exterior crust creates channels that drain flavorful juices into the fire or pan.
Cutting into steak immediately without resting: heated muscle fibers push internal juices to the center; cutting without a 5-minute rest causes juices to spill out onto the board, leaving meat dry.
avoid.source: WebstaurantStore (Resting Meat: Why You Should and for How Long)

avoid.warning: Failing to account for carryover cooking: meat continues cooking after removal from heat; remove steaks 5°F to 10°F below desired final doneness.
